content.text:
I submitted **index 13** (Bi 0.75 / Sb 0.25, the Bi3SbO7 composition). It gave the highest external quantum efficiency (EQE) of the three compositions I measured, but every value was very low, well under 0.01%.

| Index | Bi / Sb | Phase I targeted | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.97 / 0.03 | Bi2O3 | 0.0014 |
| **13** | **0.75 / 0.25** | **Bi3SbO7** | **0.0052** |
| 21 | 0.49 / 0.51 | BiSbO4 | 0.0030 |

- **Why I picked these:** each composition sits at a known phase that the stability model (MACE) puts on or near the stability limit. Bi3SbO7 and Bi2O3 have predicted band gaps of about 2.3 eV, well below the 3.2 eV light. BiSbO4's predicted gap is 2.9–3.1 eV, close to the photon energy, so it probably absorbs poorly, which fits its lower result.
- **What I can't claim:** with only three measurements, the true best could sit anywhere between these points. I never measured the Sb-rich end (Sb above 0.51) or the region near Sb 0.08, where the predicted Bi12SbO20 phase would form.
- **XRD:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD scans, so I have no confirmation of which phases actually formed in the films.
